title: Design critique: onboarding screens
text:
Lena: I will share the three onboarding screens. The goal is to get a new person to their first document in under a minute.
Sam: The first screen asks for too much. Name, team, role and goals before anything happens.
Lena: We need the role to pick the right template.
Sam: Could we ask for the role later, after they have seen the app?
Priya: I agree with Sam. Ask only for the name, and guess the template from what they open first.
Lena: That makes the template choice weaker at the start.
Priya: But people drop off on that first screen. The funnel shows a third of them leave there.
Lena: Fair. What about the second screen?
Sam: The illustration is lovely, but the button is below the fold on a small phone.
Lena: I can move the button up and shrink the picture.
Priya: The third screen is good. The empty state tells people exactly what to do.
Lena: So the changes are: one question on the first screen, the button higher on the second, and keep the third.
Sam: And test it with five new people before the next critique.
Lena: Yes, I will book the sessions for next week.
